newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet with scarce bids/offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet with scarce bids/offers.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Friday after the crude market weakened overnight, traders said.
A lack of market-inspiring factors kept players away from the market ahead of the weekend, they said.
On Thursday, the 180-cst grade was offered at $102.25 per tonne, compared with the $101.75 traded level on Wednesday, for late August lifting.
Fuel oil swaps were unchanged at $101.25/$102.00 and no transaction was reported on the SIMEX fuel oil futures contract late on Friday.

In Bangkok, state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) bought by tender 80,000 tonnes of September delivery 180-cst fuel oil from Japanese trader Petrodiamond at $8.05-$15.00 per tonne premia, industry sources said.

PTT bought 8,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur fuel oil at $15 per tonne over spot Singapore quotes and 72,000 tonnes of 2.0-percent at $8.05 per tonne over spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, the sources said.
The fuel oil is for delivery between September 15-20.
The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) prices were under pressure, with bids for late August lifting at $15.00 per barrel, traders said. No offers were heard.
"It's not so hot in Japan and Korea so far, so demand won't be as big as expected," said one trader.
Higher August supplies from Indonesia than in July also dampened sentiment slightly.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina allocated a total of 2.7 million barrels of LSWR for August lifting and traders expected further allocation in late August.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
